html:
Roman general and statesman, called Magnus, "the Great", the most famous Roman of his day until Caesar.

He began as a young supporter of Sulla, raising his own legions at 23. He fought the Sertorian War in Spain and mopped up the last of Spartacus's slaves. Consul in 70 BCE with Crassus, he then won two huge commands. In 67 BCE he cleared the Mediterranean of pirates in about three months. From 66 BCE he finished off Mithridates VI, ended the Seleucid kingdom by making Syria a province, and took Jerusalem in 63 BCE.

Back in Rome the Senate blocked his plans, so in 60 BCE he joined Caesar and Crassus in the First Triumvirate and married Caesar's daughter Julia. He built Rome's first stone theatre, the Theatre of Pompey. After Julia died in 54 BCE and Crassus in 53 BCE, he drifted to the Senate's side against Caesar.

In the civil war Caesar beat him at Pharsalus in 48 BCE. Pompey fled to Egypt, where courtiers of the young king Ptolemy XIII had him stabbed as he came ashore.
sum: Roman general and statesman, called Magnus, "the Great", the most famous Roman of his day until Caesar.
